summary: The leaf-eating larva of Beedrill, and SoulSilver's counterpart to Caterpie in Ilex Forest. Weedle carries a two-inch poison barb on its head and a bright body that warns enemies off; it hides in grass and bushes and under the leaves it eats, and it eats its own weight in leaves every day. A keen sense of smell, through a big red nose, lets it tell the leaves it likes from those it doesn't. In Ilex Forest it is met in the morning and by day, never at night.

anatomy.text: A small larva (0.3 m, 3.2 kg) with a sharp poison barb, about two inches long, on top of its head.
A big red proboscis, which the entries call its nose.
Its category is Hairy Bug Pokémon, though no entry mentions hair.

diet.text: Leaves. It is usually found under the leaves it eats, eats leaves in grass and bushes, and eats its own weight in leaves every day.
A selective feeder: it has favourite kinds of leaves and ones it dislikes, and tells them apart by smell.
diet.analogy: Real caterpillars choose food plants by taste and smell receptors on the antennae and mouthparts, and many eat only a few related plants.

diet.text: Eating its body weight daily, over 3 kg of leaves at game size, makes it a heavy leaf-eater; Caterpie's entries describe a similar appetite.

habitat.text: Forests and grasslands, in grass and bushes.

In SoulSilver it is in Ilex Forest's grass (50% of encounters in the morning, 60% by day, none at night) and common Headbutt trees (30%), on Routes 30 and 31, in National Park, and in Kanto on Route 2 and in Viridian Forest. In HeartGold it appears only in the Bug-Catching Contest, and Caterpie takes its slots.
Its microhabitat is low and sheltered: grass, bushes and the undersides of leaves.

behavior.text: It hides, in grass and bushes and under its food leaves.
In Ilex Forest it is met only in the morning and by day; SoulSilver's Route 2 tables also have it at night (10%), so it isn't strictly diurnal. This rests on the time-of-day split in the tables only.

social.text: No entry describes groups, pairs or any dealings with its own kind.

reproduction.text: Bug egg group, 15 egg cycles, an even sex ratio. Nothing in the Pokédex describes eggs or where they are laid.

defense.text: A venomous barb on its head: very powerful, it secretes a strong poison and injects it.
defense.analogy: Real venomous caterpillars, such as slug moth (Limacodidae) and flannel moth (Megalopygidae) larvae, deliver venom through many hollow spines rather than one barb.

defense.text: Warning colours: its bright body is meant to warn enemies off.
defense.analogy: Aposematism: a conspicuous colour paired with a real defence, which predators such as birds learn to avoid.

defense.text: It fends off attackers with the needle, and attacks with it too.
Poison Sting (Lv 1) is the barb in game form; its ability, Shield Dust, blocks the added effects of attacks taken.

senses.text: An extremely acute sense of smell, through its big red nose, good enough to sort favourite leaves from disliked ones.
The capability records turn this into tracking (following a scent), but no entry says it follows anything except leaves.

life_cycle.text: Weedle becomes Kakuna at level 7, and Kakuna becomes Beedrill at level 10: larva, pupa, adult.
Larva and adult lead opposite lives: Weedle eats leaves, Beedrill hunts prey with its stings and carries victims to its nest.
The larva lives free among leaves, not in Beedrill's nest: it is found under the leaves it eats. Whatever Beedrill's nest is provisioned for, it isn't Weedle's food.
life_cycle.analogy: Among real Hymenoptera only sawflies have free-living, leaf-eating, caterpillar-like larvae, and adult sawflies don't sting; stinging wasps and bees raise legless grubs that are fed in a nest. The Weedle line combines a sawfly-type larva with a stinging, nest-provisioning adult.

life_cycle.text: Kakuna hides under leaves and in nooks of branches, close to where Weedle feeds, so the larva probably pupates near its food plants.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Poison Sting and String Shot are its moves from hatching. Bug Bite comes at level 15, but it becomes Kakuna at 7, so a wild Weedle stings and spins, and that's all.
String Shot is presumably the silk it pupates in, though no Weedle or Kakuna entry mentions silk.
moves_in_the_wild.note: By analogy with Caterpie's cocoon (10.8), not from any Weedle-line entry.

moves_in_the_wild.text: The line has no egg moves in HeartGold and SoulSilver.

ecology.text: A primary consumer of leaves (trophic level 2) in SoulSilver's Ilex Forest, chemically defended, which should make it a poor meal for predators that have learned its colours.
Its choosy palate could shape which plants get eaten in the understory, but its food plants aren't named.
ecology.note: Nothing says which leaves it prefers or how much damage it does.

ecology.text: The Weedle line routes leaf energy into a predator (Beedrill), where the Caterpie line routes it into a flower-visitor (Butterfree). The two versions of Ilex Forest differ by that one switch.

humans.text: People are told to beware the stinger on its head.
Easy to catch (catch rate 255) and common on Johto's first routes in SoulSilver.

homestead.text: Not a garden helper: it eats its own weight in leaves daily. Its choosiness might make it easier to keep off crops it dislikes, but nobody knows which those are.
Its nose sorts leaves by smell; whether that could be put to sorting forage for people has never been described.
homestead.note: Its smell is only ever described in the service of its own diet.

homestead.text: The capability records list Weedle under light because 13.3 calls its body 'bright-colored'. That means conspicuous, not luminous; it gives no light.
Handle with gloves: the head barb injects a strong poison.

niche.foraging: selective leaf-eating, choosing leaves by smell, hidden under its food

relationships.note: Both larvae eat leaves in the same forest; the games never let them share Ilex Forest in one version and give each the other's slots at the same rates. Read as competitive exclusion it is a hypothesis resting on a version-exclusive design device.
Together only in National Park's Bug-Catching Contest, in both versions.

Both in Ilex Forest's common Headbutt trees; warning colours imply predators that learn. Against it: Hoothoot's grass records are at night and Weedle's by day, and the barb makes it a risky meal. Hoothoot's diet isn't stated.
Noctowl catches prey in darkness and shares the forest's trees; a resting larva at night is within reach. Prey is never named.
Carnivine (the 'Bug Catcher Pokémon') dangles from branches to ambush prey; it is in Ilex Forest only when the Sinnoh Sound plays on the radio.
Same grass, opposite shifts: Weedle morning and day, Oddish night only.

open_questions: Which leaves does it favour, and which does it reject?
Is its poison made by Weedle itself or taken from the plants it eats?
Does it ever live in or near Beedrill's nest?
Why is it met at night on SoulSilver's Route 2 but never in Ilex Forest?
What learns to avoid its warning colours? No predator is named.
The line has no HeartGold-SoulSilver egg moves, so no ecotypes can be read from breeding.
